theory.intro: When the volume is given and a measurement is missing, substitute the volume and every known measurement into $V = Ah$. Solve for the unknown using inverse operations.
facts: Substitute **first**: put the volume and the known measurements into $V = Ah$, and the letter still showing is the unknown.
In $V = Ah$, $A$ is the area of the uniform cross-section and $h$ is the distance between the two parallel cross-sections.
Finding the distance between cross-sections or the cross-sectional area needs one **division**: $h = \frac{V}{A}$ and $A = \frac{V}{h}$.
For a rectangular prism, first find the known rectangular cross-section area using $A = lw$, then divide the volume by that area to find the missing length.
For a cube of side length $x$, $V = x^{3}$. Find the side length by taking the cube root of the volume.
A length answer uses cm, m or mm. A cross-sectional-area answer uses square units such as cm², m² or mm².
When solids have equal volumes, calculate the volume of the fully measured solid first, then use that volume to find the missing measurement of the other solid.
Only a positive side length is used.
Carry values exactly through the working and round only at the last line, to the form the question asks for.
steps: Substitute the volume and the known dimensions.

workedExamples.question_text: A prism has a uniform cross-sectional area of $14\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a volume of $119\text{ cm}^{3}$. Find the distance $h$ between its parallel cross-sections.
A prism has a volume of $102\text{ mm}^{3}$. The distance between its parallel cross-sections is $6\text{ mm}$. Find the area $A$ of its uniform cross-section.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the $7\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ face as the cross-section.
$\begin{align*}A &= 7\times4\\&=28\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}V &= Ax\\168 &=28x\\x &=\frac{168}{28}\\x &=6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A cube has a volume of $200\text{ cm}^{3}$. Find its side length $x$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
Two rectangular prisms have the same volume. Prism A has dimensions $x\text{ cm}$, $5\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$. Prism B has dimensions $8\text{ cm}$, $6\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$. Find $x$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Prism B:
$\begin{align*}V &= (8\times6)\times5\\&=240\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$
Prism A:
$\begin{align*}A &=5\times3\\&=15\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}V &=Ax\\240 &=15x\\x &=\frac{240}{15}\\x &=16\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular prism measures $16\text{ cm}$ by $9\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$. Its volume is double the volume of a cube with side length $x\text{ cm}$. Find $x$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Rectangular prism:
$\begin{align*}V &=(16\times9)\times5\\&=720\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$
The cube has half this volume.
$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cube}} &=720\div2\\&=360\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}360 &=x^{3}\\x &=\sqrt[3]{360}\\&=7.1137\ldots\\&\approx7.11\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

foundation.question_text:
A prism has a uniform cross-sectional area of $25\text{ mm}^{2}$ and a volume of $225\text{ mm}^{3}$.
Find the distance $h$ between its parallel cross-sections, in mm.

A prism has a volume of $60\text{ cm}^{3}$ and the distance between its parallel cross-sections is $5\text{ cm}$.
Find the area $A$ of its uniform cross-section, in cm².

A rectangular prism has a volume of $150\text{ m}^{3}$. Its rectangular base measures $5\text{ m}$ by $6\text{ m}$.
Find its height $h$, in m.

A rectangular prism has a volume of $144\text{ cm}^{3}$. Two of its dimensions are $4\text{ cm}$ and $6\text{ cm}$.
Find the missing dimension $x$, in cm.

development.question_text:
A rectangular concrete slab is $6$ m long and $4$ m wide, and contains $3.6$ m³ of concrete.
Find the thickness of the slab, in m.

A copper bar is a prism with a uniform cross-sectional area of $18$ cm² and a volume of $459$ cm³.
Find the length of the bar, in cm.

A prism has a uniform cross-sectional area of $16.8\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a volume of $315\text{ cm}^{3}$.
Find the distance $h$ between its parallel cross-sections, in cm.

A prism has a volume of $93.6\text{ cm}^{3}$ and the distance between its parallel cross-sections is $7.2\text{ cm}$.
Find the area $A$ of its uniform cross-section, in cm².

A cube has a volume of $343\text{ cm}^{3}$.
Find its side length $x$, in cm.

A rectangular prism has a volume of $157.5\text{ m}^{3}$. Its rectangular base measures $4.5\text{ m}$ by $5\text{ m}$.
Find its height $h$, in m.

development.solution_text:
Prism B: $V = (15 \times 4) \times 8$
$= 480\text{ cm}^{3}$
Prism A: $A = 4 \times 10$
$= 40\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$480 = 40x$
$x = 12\text{ cm}$

development.question_text:
Two rectangular prisms have the same volume. Prism A has dimensions $x\text{ cm}$, $6\text{ cm}$ and $4\text{ cm}$. Prism B has dimensions $9\text{ cm}$, $5\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$.
Find the value of $x$, in cm.
development.solution_text:
Prism B: $V = (9 \times 5) \times 8$
$= 360\text{ cm}^{3}$
Prism A: $A = 6 \times 4$
$= 24\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$360 = 24x$
$x = 15\text{ cm}$

mastery.question_text:
A cube has a volume of $500\text{ cm}^{3}$.
Find its side length $x$, in cm, correct to $2$ decimal places.

Two rectangular prisms have the same volume. Prism A has dimensions $x\text{ cm}$, $3.6\text{ cm}$ and $2.5\text{ cm}$. Prism B has dimensions $7.5\text{ cm}$, $4.8\text{ cm}$ and $6.2\text{ cm}$.
Find the value of $x$, in cm.
mastery.solution_text:
Prism B: $V = (7.5 \times 4.8) \times 6.2$
$= 223.2\text{ cm}^{3}$
Prism A: $A = 3.6 \times 2.5$
$= 9\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$223.2 = 9x$
$x = 24.8\text{ cm}$

mastery.question_text:
A rectangular prism has dimensions $18\text{ cm}$, $15\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$. Its volume is double the volume of a cube of side length $x\text{ cm}$.
Find the value of $x$, in cm, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
Rectangular prism: $V = (18 \times 15) \times 8$
$= 2160\text{ cm}^{3}$
Cube: $V = 2160 \div 2$
$= 1080\text{ cm}^{3}$
$1080 = x^{3}$
$x = \sqrt[3]{1080}$
$= 10.2598\ldots$
$\approx 10.26\text{ cm}$

mastery.question_text:
A cube has a volume of $6.4\text{ m}^{3}$.
Find its side length $x$, in m, correct to $2$ decimal places.
